title: Accrued revenue

match.reason: The closest bank points teach that revenue is earned when delivered, but none covers recording accrued revenue as an asset at balance day and clearing it when cash arrives, which is a new step at a deeper Units 3 and 4 level.

draft.title: Accrued revenue
card: Accrued revenue is revenue a business has earned by balance day but has not yet received in cash. The service has been done, but the money has not arrived.
On balance day, record the revenue in the period it was earned. Debit an asset account such as Accrued revenue (or Accounts receivable), and credit the revenue account.
The asset shows that the business is owed money. Revenue is higher in the period it was earned, even though no cash has come in.
In the next period, when the cash arrives, debit Cash at bank and credit the asset account. This clears the asset. No revenue is recorded again, as it was already counted.
draft.remember: Earned but not received: record revenue and an asset now, then clear the asset when the cash arrives.

a.q: On 30 June, Priya's Tutoring has earned $600 in fees that the client will pay in July. How is this recorded on 30 June?
opts: Debit Accrued revenue, credit Fee revenue
Debit Cash at bank, credit Fee revenue
Debit Fee revenue, credit Accrued revenue
Debit Accrued revenue, credit Cash at bank
a.why: The fees are earned in June, so revenue is credited. The business is owed $600, so an asset is debited. Cash at bank is wrong because no cash has been received yet.
a.clue: Money is owed to the business, and no cash has come in.

b.q: Leon's Landscaping mowed a client's lawns in June and will be paid $900 in July. In July the cash arrives. What is recorded in July?
opts: Debit Cash at bank, credit Accrued revenue
Debit Cash at bank, credit Fee revenue
Debit Accrued revenue, credit Fee revenue
Debit Accrued revenue, credit Cash at bank
b.why: The revenue was recorded in June, so in July the cash clears the asset: debit Cash at bank and credit Accrued revenue. Crediting Fee revenue is tempting, but it would count the same revenue twice.
b.clue: The revenue was already recorded in June.

a.best: Debit Accrued revenue, credit Fee revenue

b.best: Debit Cash at bank, credit Accrued revenue

problems.detail: The card offers 'Accrued revenue (or Accounts receivable)' as interchangeable for the balance day entry. In VCE Accounting, Accrued revenue is its own current asset account for revenue earned but not yet received. Accounts receivable is recorded at the time of an invoiced credit sale, not as a balance day adjustment. Offering it as an alternative may confuse students in exams.

The stem never says that a balance day adjustment was recorded on 30 June, or that June is the end of the reporting period. Without the clue, 'Debit Cash at bank, credit Fee revenue' is defensible. The stem should state that accrued revenue of $900 was recorded on 30 June.

check.summary: Both intended answers are correct. The card wrongly suggests Accounts receivable can replace Accrued revenue in the balance day entry. Question b's stem should say the accrued revenue was recorded on 30 June, rather than leaving that to the clue.
